name: Rice Bacterial Blight
description: The most serious bacterial disease of rice worldwide, causing leaf blighting and seedling wilt. It is favored by high rainfall, deep water, and high nitrogen fertilization. Bacterial blight can cause yield losses of up to 50% in susceptible varieties.
symptoms: Water-soaked yellow stripes along leaf veins
Stripes turning white to gray with wavy margins
Lesions extending the entire leaf length in severe infections
Leaves drying and turning white or pale yellow
Kresek phase: seedling wilting and death within weeks of transplanting
Yellow bacterial exudate on lesions in wet mornings
causes: Rain splash and floodwater dispersing bacteria
High nitrogen fertilization creating susceptible growth
Continuous rice cropping with infected crop residue
treatments: Apply copper-based bactericides at first symptoms
Reduce nitrogen application during disease development
Drain fields where possible to reduce spread
Spray streptomycin where registered and available
prevention: Use balanced nitrogen fertilization — avoid excess
Remove and destroy crop residue after harvest
Avoid deep water in fields during susceptible stages
references: Africa Rice Center Bacterial Blight Manual
